children.topic: Clinical Signs: Left upper quadrant tenderness, pleuritic chest pain
Diagnostic Modality: Contrast-Enhanced Abdominal CT (Gold Standard)
Treatment: Observation (if no active bleed) or Splenic Artery Embolization (if active contrast 'blush' present)
Clinical Signs: Kehr's Sign (referred left shoulder pain), Balance's Sign (fixed left flank dullness, shifting right dullness)
Diagnostic Modality: FAST or urgent DPL (if FAST equivocal/unavailable)
Treatment: Immediate Exploratory Laparotomy & Splenectomy (or splenorrhaphy if salvageable)
Clinical Signs: Initial trauma shock → Lucid interval up to 15 days → Sudden blowout
Diagnostic Modality: Repeat abdominal CT scan with contrast
Treatment: Urgent laparotomy, resuscitation, and surgical decompression
Risk: High-risk rapid sepsis from encapsulated bacteria (S. pneumoniae, N. meningitidis, H. influenzae)
Treatment: Triple Vaccine Protocol (ideally 2 weeks post-op or prior to discharge) + oral amoxicillin for 2 years in pediatric patients
